quote: After these, in the seventh month other solemnities are kept. On the "first day of the month" the new moon of the trumpets, as it says in the Psalm: "sound the trumpet at the beginning of the month". But on the "tenth day of the seventh month" is this solemnity of atonement. "On this" day alone the high priest is clothed with all the priestly garments, then he is clothed with "manifestation and truth", then he enters into those inaccessible places, whither it is permitted to approach only "once in the year", that is, into the "holy of holies". For "once in the year" the high priest, leaving the people, enters into that place where is the "propitiatory" and above the "propitiatory" the "cherubim", where is also the "ark of testimony" and the "altar of incense", whither it is lawful for no one to enter except the high priest alone.

Then next follows the festival of the sevenths. For just as among the days every seventh day is observed as a sabbath and is a festival, so also among the months every seventh month is the sabbath of the months. There is therefore kept in it the festival which is called the sabbath of sabbaths, and on the first day of the month there is made the memorial of trumpets. But who is it that keeps the festival of the memorial of trumpets, except he who is able to commit to memory the prophetic and evangelical and apostolic scriptures, which sound forth like a certain heavenly trumpet, and to store them up within the treasury of his heart? He therefore who does this, and meditates on the law of God day and night, this man keeps the festival of the memorial of trumpets. But also, if anyone is able to merit those graces of the Holy Spirit by which the prophets were inspired, and to say, singing…

There is still also another festival, when they afflict their souls and humble themselves, celebrating festivals to God. O wondrous festival: the affliction of the soul is called a feast day! "For this," He says, "is the day of propitiation, on the tenth day of the seventh month." See, therefore, if you wish to keep a feast day, if you wish that God rejoice over you, afflict your soul and humble it. Do not permit it to fulfill its desires, nor grant it to wander off into wantonness, but as far as can be done, afflict and humble it. Finally, both the festival of the Passover and that of the unleavened bread is said to have the bread of affliction, nor can anyone keep a feast day unless he has eaten the bread of affliction, and has eaten the pasch with bitterness. "For you shall eat," He says, "the unleavened bread with bitterness," or with bitter herbs. You see, therefore, of what sort…

All who are to be trained in the higher disciplines regard the labor of the rudiments as burdensome, so long as they do not know what the end and fruit of that discipline is to which they are being introduced. But when, having been led through in order, the perfection of the discipline has been attained, then it will be a delight to have endured the burdens of the rudiments. There are, therefore, also in holy and divine matters certain first rudiments, by which those are introduced who strive toward the perfection of blessedness. This the servant of God clearly indicates in the song of Exodus, saying: "Bringing them in, plant them on the mountain of your inheritance, in your prepared dwelling, which you have prepared, O Lord." Paul the Apostle also, knowing that there are certain first beginnings of instruction, and that then afterward, in the course of time, one comes even to…

But now let us see what is the last feast day of God, on which God rejoices in man. "Tabernacles," He says. He rejoices, then, over you when He sees you dwelling in this world in tents, when He sees you not having your mind and purpose fixed and founded upon the earth, nor desiring the things that are earthly, nor reckoning the shadow of this life as your own perpetual possession, but as though set in transit and hastening to that true fatherland of paradise, whence you came forth, and saying: "I am a sojourner and a pilgrim, as all my fathers." For the fathers too dwelt in tents, and Abraham dwelt in little huts, that is, in tents, with Isaac and Jacob, coheirs of the same promise. When, therefore, you have been a sojourner and a pilgrim on the earth, and your mind is not fixed and rooted in the desires of earthly things, but you are ready to pass over quickly and ready to stretch…
